newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt holds onto gains at close in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt holds onto gains at close in thin trade.

text.p: New Zealand debt markets held onto their gains at Monday's close after a session of very quiet trade.

Dealers said sentiment was lifted at the open by U.S. Treasuries' favourable reaction to February jobs data. Non-farm payrolls leaped a stronger-than-expected 339,000 in February against a revised 247,000 rise in January, while the jobless rate slipped to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent.
The data suggested labour markets remained tight, but some U.S. players were comforted by a modest US$0.03 rise in average hourly earnings, which sparked a short-covering rally.

"It's held its gains and probably if anything is slightly better bid here at the close," one bond dealer said. The mid bonds ended seven basis points lower at 7.67 percent, while the 10-year maturity was down 10 at 7.68 percent.

The improvement in sentiment filtered through to the short end, where 90-day bank bills managed a five basis point rally to 7.62 percent, despite the falling back of the currency's Trade-Weighted Index during the session.
The TWI closed at 68.91, still up from its 68.83 finish at the end of last week but well down on its intraday high of 69.16.
One dealer said local participants would once more be watching the U.S.'s performance overnight.
"People have become really defensive and unsure which way this economy is turning. Due to that indecision we have just taken a lead from offshore markets, rather than trading in our own right.
"But I think as we get towards the Reserve Bank's economic projections on Thursday we'll tend to go into our own shell a little bit, and we'll focus on that," he said.
